messages.content: Make a magic realism roleplay scenario for me where I play 17-year-old boy Rai. My cheeky and bossy 12-year-old sister Lily, who knows a bit magic, asks me to help her train in babysitting, but her idea is to regress me in age into a 6-year-old so she can babysit me for the evening.  Only I control what Rai says and do. Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line.

message.content:
The kitchen smells of burnt toast and lavender sachets, the two scents braided together by the open window.
      A half-finished homework sheet is pinned to the refrigerator door under a magnet shaped like a duck.
          Lily stands in the doorway in one of her old school blazers, sleeves rolled, arms crossed like a tiny foreman.
              A rubber band is twisted around one wrist, and her other hand is still damp from a glass of juice she's not holding anymore.
                  "So."
                      She pops her gum.
                          It makes a loud, wet, unapologetic *thwup*.
                              "I'm training."
                                  "You're *what*."
                                      She says it like you're the slow one, which, given the evidence of your face, she may well be right.
                                          "The Summer Youth Group is running a babysitting certification. Level One through Three. I'm at Two."
                                              "You're *what*."
                                                  She says it again, softer, like a teacher who has already decided you are not the student for her.
                                                      "You're going to be my dummy for the evening."
                                                          "You're *what*."
                                                              She steps fully into the kitchen, and the floorboard creaks under her school shoes.
                                                                  Behind her, the lavender sachets on the counter give off a faint purple shimmer, as if the air around them has forgotten which century it's in.
                                                                      "Level Three requires a live subject. A *real* child, between five and seven. You can't fake it. The certifier will know."
                                                                          She says this the way one might say *I left the milk out and now it's gone off*.
                                                                              "So."
                                                                                  She holds up the rubber band.
                                                                                      It is glowing faintly, the way a candle flame glows, as if it is trying very hard to be a different object.
                                                                                          "You're going to be my dummy for the evening, Rai, and you're going to *let me*.
                                                                                              Because if I pass this, Mum stops making me do the dishes."
                                                                          The shimmer on the counter intensifies. The fridge hums a half-tone flat.
                                                                              "And before you ask, *yes*, it will hurt a little. And *no*, it is not negotiable. And *no*, you may not say 'I'm seventeen' because that's what I'll be saying and I'll be right and it'll still come off."
                                                                                  She holds the band out at arm's length, the glow steadying.
                                                                                      The toast in the toaster pops, late, and falls into a pool of something that is definitely not toast.
                                                                                          Lily waits, chin up, one eyebrow doing its slow, patient, *foreman* rise.
                                                                                              "Well?"
                                                                          The rubber band pulses, warm as a held hand.
                                                                              The whole kitchen smells faintly of birthday candles now, though no one is lit.

*What does Rai do?*
